overall: The AG found the Board violated the OML by failing to timely approve five of seven sets of minutes, found the violation intentional, declined a civil penalty, and ordered compliance and member training.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to timely approve seven sets of minutes of meetings held between October 2022 and May 2023.
allegations.key_passage: However, we find that the minutes of the meetings held on October 12, 2022, March 8, 2023, March 15, 2023, March 29, 2023, and April 12, 2023, were not approved in a timely manner where the minutes were not approved within the later of the next three meetings or 30 days following each meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged untimely approval of minutes from the April 26 and May 3, 2023 meetings, which the Board approved on May 17, 2023.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law with respect to these two sets of minutes.

allegations.summary: Whether the untimely approval of minutes was an intentional violation of the Open Meeting Law, as the complainant urged.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Board had previously been advised that the failure to approve minutes within the next three meetings or 30 days, whichever is longer, violates the Open Meeting Law, we find that this violation is intentional.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
All members of the Board to attend a webinar training on the Open Meeting Law conducted by the AG's office within 90 days.
remedy_passage: We order the Board's immediate and future compliance with the law's requirements and caution the Board that a future finding of an intentional violation of the Open Meeting Law may result in a civil penalty of up to $1,000 per violation. In addition, we order all members of the Board to attend a webinar training on the Open Meeting Law conducted by our office within the next 90 days.
